clips.send: A parent sends it to anyone who was told their number was fine - the number doesn't predict the blockage, and the anxiety underneath it.
clips.caption:
Kevin Trudeau points out something most people never hear from their own doctor: a cholesterol count doesn't reliably predict a blocked artery.

Some people test at 600 or 700 and live for decades with clean arteries. Others test very low and still end up fully blocked. Same test, opposite outcomes - which means the number alone isn't telling the whole story.

His point isn't to throw out your numbers. It's to ask what else is actually happening in your arteries before you accept one number as the whole answer.

What would you ask your doctor about your own numbers?
